# Causal design memo: home water-use reports trial

**Recommendation:** treat this as the cluster-randomized trial it is. Compare the 12 report towns with the 12 control towns over March 2025–February 2026, use each household's pre-trial use only to improve precision, and base inference on the 24-town random draw.

Your analyst's plan has three problems:

- **The before/after comparison cannot isolate the reports.** The July 2025 drought order, seasonality, weather and any other change during the trial all move use in the same window. The control towns are the only comparison that removes them, and the random draw is what makes that comparison fair.
- **Rebate sign-up should not be a control.** The reports caused part of the extra sign-up, so controlling for it removes part of the effect the board is asking about. It can also bias the estimate through unmeasured conservation motivation.
- **The standard errors will not be tiny.** Treatment was assigned to 24 towns, not 2.1 million reads. Reads from the same household are correlated, and so are households in the same town. The precision limit is about 12 towns against 12, so the inference must work at the town level.

I couldn't write the file in this turn. Here is the path and full text.

**Path:** `home-water-reports/causal-design.md`

```markdown
# Causal design: effect of monthly home water-use reports (2025 trial)

Pre-estimation memo. No data have been inspected; nothing has been fitted. Every
diagnostic below is planned, not performed. Facts come from the partner's
description unless marked "assumed".

## 1. Decision and requested estimand

**Primary recommendation:** analyze the trial as a cluster-randomized trial,
comparing report towns with control towns. This is an intention-to-treat (ITT)
comparison of mailing the reports.
- Unit of assignment: the town (12 of 24 drawn at random).
- Outcome: household water use, March 2025 – February 2026.
- Baseline adjustment: the household's pre-trial use, for precision only.
- Inference: randomization inference based on the actual draw, with
  small-sample cluster-robust inference as a secondary check.

Do not use the single-arm before/after design, and do not adjust for rebate
sign-up.

- **Requested causal question:**
  - Intervention: monthly mailed neighbor-comparison reports to every household
    in a town, starting March 2025.
  - Comparator: no reports (status quo).
  - Outcome: household metered water use (units to confirm; assumed gallons per
    month).
  - Population: households in the 24 smart-meter trial towns.
  - Time zero and horizon: March 2025, with follow-up through February 2026
    (12 months).
  - Contrast: mean difference in average monthly use per household. A percent
    reduction relative to the control arm is a secondary scale.
  - Decision: assumed to be whether to continue or expand the reports. The
    decision has not been stated (see §9).
- **Requested estimand:** the ITT effect of *mailing* the reports. It is the
  difference in mean monthly household use over the 12 months between two
  scenarios: all trial towns are mailed reports, versus none are. Because the
  draw was random, this equals, in expectation, the effect in the 12 report
  towns, which is the board's "did it cut use in the trial towns".
- **What the estimand does not cover:**
  - Reading the reports: there is no record of who read them, so that effect is
    not identified.
  - The 34 non-trial towns.
  - Use in the absence of a drought order. The trial ran under the July 2025
    order, so the effect is the effect of reports in that context.
- **Design status:** `plausibly identified`.
  - Random assignment of towns gives the comparison as-if-random exchangeability.
  - Mailing was universal in report towns and opt-out was impossible, so
    assignment and the mailing intervention coincide.
  - Gates to confirm: the randomization record (§9 Q1), the household cohort
    definition (Q3), and that nothing else differed systematically by arm (Q2, Q5).
- **Supported alternative estimands (separate; none replaces the primary):**
  - (a) ITT effect on rebate sign-up. Plausibly identified by the same design.
  - (b) Effect of reports by period (before vs. after the drought order). This is
    descriptive heterogeneity, because the timing of the order was not
    randomized.
  - (c) Effect *not via* rebates, a controlled direct effect. It is a mediation
    target and is **not identified** without additional assumptions about what
    drives rebate sign-up.
  - (d) Effect if reports went to all 58 towns. **Not identified** from the trial
    alone: smart-meter towns were selected, not sampled, so this needs a
    transport argument.
- **Recommendation-changing conditions:**
  - The draw was stratified or matched: the inference must follow the actual
    design.
  - Control towns received reports or a similar program: the contrast and the
    estimand change.
  - The rebate program, rates or drought rules differed by arm for reasons other
    than the reports: there is a concurrent-event threat, so investigate before
    estimating.
  - Arm-level outcome results have already been viewed: prespecify regardless,
    and disclose this.
  - Estimation should wait for the confirmations in §9 Q1–Q3. These are
    record checks, not new data collection.

Sources: Hernán and Robins (2020) on ITT, randomization and adjustment for
post-treatment variables.

## 2. Design and data inventory

| Fact | Status | Evidence | Implication/action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 smart-meter towns chosen for the trial, out of 58 | Known | Partner | Trial population = these 24 towns; results do not transport automatically to the other 34 |
| 12 of 24 towns drawn at random for reports | Known | Partner | Cluster randomization; obtain the draw record (method, seed, any strata, date) |
| Complete randomization of 12 of 24, no strata, single draw before March 2025 | **Assumed** | None | Sets the randomization-inference reference set; confirm (Q1) |
| Towns are separate communities at least 10 miles apart | Known | Partner | Cross-town spillover is plausibly small; within-town spillover is part of the town-level intervention |
| Reports were mailed monthly from March 2025 to every household in report towns; no opt-out | Known | Partner | Mailing = assignment; no noncompliance in mailing |
| Every scheduled mailing went out and reached households (no batch failures) | **Assumed** | None | Confirm mailing logs (Q2); a failed batch is a version/consistency issue, not a reason to drop the town |
| Control towns got no reports or similar conservation mailings | Known for reports; **assumed** for other mailings | Partner | Confirm (Q2) |
| No record of who read the reports | Known | Partner | The effect of reading is not identified; only the mailing ITT is |
| Monthly meter reads for all households in the 24 towns, Mar 2023 – Feb 2026, ~2.1M reads (~58k households if most have 36 months; approximation) | Known (count); household count inferred | Partner | 24 pre-trial months support a baseline covariate and placebo checks; precision is limited by 24 towns |
| Household size and lot size from billing records | Known | Partner | Usable only if measured before March 2025; confirm timing (Q4) |
| Drought order limiting lawn watering in all 58 towns from July 2025 | Known | Partner | Affects both arms; removed by the between-arm contrast. Defines the context of the effect. Confirm uniform rules and enforcement (Q6) |
| Rebate sign-up for low-flow fixtures, higher in report towns | Known (direction); magnitude unknown | Partner | Post-treatment mediator; exclude from the adjustment set; analyze as a secondary outcome |
| Rebate program offered equally in all 24 towns, and its eligibility/advertising did not differ by arm except via the reports | **Assumed** | None | If the reports advertised the rebate, the rebate is part of the intervention (fine for ITT); confirm (Q5) |
| Household definition (account vs. premise), movers, new connections, master-metered buildings | Unknown | None | Define a baseline cohort (§7); check churn by arm |
| Missing or estimated reads, meter replacements, read-cycle dates, units | Unknown | None | Check by arm; misaligned billing periods affect March 2025 exposure |
| Other town-specific events during the trial (rate changes, main breaks, local campaigns) | Unknown | None | Inventory by arm (Q6) |
| Whether arm-level outcomes have already been examined | Unknown | None | Affects prespecification credibility (Q8) |

No data were inspected. Field roles:
- Town T and household i (keys).
- Assignment Z_T (report town = 1), set before March 2025.
- Monthly use Y_it for each month t; pre-period Mar 2023 – Feb 2025, follow-up
  Mar 2025 – Feb 2026.
- Household size H and lot size L (baseline, timing to confirm).
- Rebate sign-up R_it (post-treatment).
- Read status (actual, estimated or missing).

Additional data required:
- Randomization record.
- Mailing logs.
- Rebate program records with dates.
- Account/premise history (move-ins and move-outs).
- Drought-order and rate-change history by town.

## 3. Causal structure and adjustment

Edge list (timing in brackets):

- Z_T [assigned before Mar 2025] -> Mail_T [Mar 2025 onward]. Deterministic:
  every household in a report town is mailed.
- Mail_T -> Read_i [unobserved] -> Y_i,post.
- Mail_T -> R_i (rebate sign-up) [post] -> Y_i,post. The reports may prompt
  sign-up, which lowers use.
- U_i (conservation motivation, income; unobserved) -> R_i, U_i -> Y_i,pre,
  U_i -> Y_i,post.
- H_i, L_i [baseline] -> Y_i,pre, Y_i,post. L_i -> lawn-watering share, which
  the drought order affects.
- Town factors V_T (climate, demographics, prices; partly unobserved)
  -> Y_i,pre, Y_i,post. **Absent edge by design: V_T -/-> Z_T**, because the
  draw was random.
- Drought order D_t [Jul 2025, all towns] -> Y_i,post. **Absent edge by design:
  D -/-> Z_T**; the order applies to both arms.
- Season and weather W_t -> Y_it in both arms.
- Mail_T -> Y of neighboring households within the town (social spillover).
  This is included in the town-level estimand.
- Disputed edge: Mail_T -> Y in control towns (cross-town spillover). Assumed
  absent because towns are at least 10 miles apart and separate communities.
- Selection: Z_T -> Stay_i (remaining in the cohort or having reads) is assumed
  negligible. Check it (§6) because it is a selection node.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Z[Z_T random draw] --> M[Mail_T]
    M --> Rd[Read_i unobserved]
    Rd --> Ypost[Y_i post]
    M --> R[Rebate sign-up R_i]
    R --> Ypost
    U[U_i motivation unobserved] --> R
    U --> Ypre[Y_i pre]
    U --> Ypost
    HL[H_i, L_i baseline] --> Ypre
    HL --> Ypost
    V[V_T town factors] --> Ypre
    V --> Ypost
    D[Drought order Jul 2025] --> Ypost
    W[Season/weather] --> Ypre
    W --> Ypost
    Z --> S[Has reads / in cohort]
```

**Target pathway:** every path from Z_T to Y_post, including the paths through
reading and through rebates.

**Adjustment set:** none is required for identification, because randomization
blocks back-door paths. Adjust for the following for **precision only**, all
measured before March 2025:
- Household pre-period use (mean monthly use Mar 2024 – Feb 2025, and
  Mar 2023 – Feb 2024).
- H_i and L_i, if measured at baseline.
- Any strata used in the draw.

**Excluded:**
- R_i (rebate sign-up): a mediator. Conditioning on it blocks part of the
  effect. It also opens Z -> R <- U -> Y, a collider path, because sign-up is
  driven by both the reports and motivation.
- H and L if they were updated after March 2025: post-treatment values.
- Read_i: unobserved and post-treatment.
- Drought-period indicators as controls: common to both arms, so they add
  nothing to identification. Month fixed effects are fine.

**Not encoded by the graph:**
- Consistency: the "reports" intervention was one version. Content changes
  over time, such as adding drought messaging after July, are part of the
  version.
- No cross-town interference.
- The cohort definition does not depend on assignment.

## 4. Identification assumptions and evidence

| Assumption | Why needed | Supporting evidence | Planned challenge | Untestable remainder / gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomization: Z_T independent of town potential outcomes | Exchangeability between arms | Partner states a random draw | Obtain the record; baseline comparison of pre-period use by arm (descriptive) | Gate: confirm the draw procedure. Baseline balance cannot prove randomization; chance imbalance with 24 towns is expected and is handled by baseline adjustment, not re-drawing |
| Consistency: mailing is a well-defined intervention | Effect has meaning | Universal monthly mailing, no opt-out | Mailing logs; report content history | Content changes define a time-varying version; record them, do not split the target |
| No cross-town interference | Control towns represent "no reports" | 10+ mile separation, separate communities | Ask about shared media, employers, regional news coverage of the reports | Untestable from use data; if it is present, the ITT is biased toward zero |
| No arm-specific concurrent events | Between-arm contrast isolates the reports | Drought order applied to all 58 towns | Inventory of rate changes, local campaigns and infrastructure events by town; leave-one-town-out | Undocumented town shocks remain possible; with only 12 per arm, one shock can matter |
| Outcome observation and cohort not affected by assignment | Comparable populations at follow-up | Smart meters read every household | Missing/estimated reads, meter swaps and churn by arm and month | Similar rates do not prove ignorable missingness; if they differ, use sensitivity analysis or bounds (§6) |
| Support | Both arms observed | 12 towns per arm, all households mailed in report towns | None needed beyond record checks | Not a concern for the trial-town ITT |
| Transport to 58 towns (alternative (d) only) | Board extrapolation | None | Compare smart-meter vs. other towns on baseline use, size, lot size | Not identified without effect-modifier and selection evidence |

**Identification vs. precision.** The ITT is identified by the random draw, but
its precision depends mainly on how much town-average outcomes vary across the
24 towns after baseline adjustment. It does not depend on the read count.
Ignoring within-town and within-household correlation would understate the
uncertainty badly.

## 5. Candidate comparison and primary choice

| Candidate | Identified estimand | Match to request | Critical assumptions | Required data | Main threat | Feasibility / failure action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Cluster-randomized ITT with baseline adjustment (primary)** | Effect of mailing on mean monthly use, trial towns, Mar 2025 – Feb 2026 | Direct | Randomization, consistency, no cross-town spillover, no arm-specific shocks, ignorable read missingness | Reads by household-month, town assignment, baseline covariates | Few clusters → wide intervals; a single town-specific shock | Feasible now. If arm-specific events are found, report with that town excluded as sensitivity and flag the result as conditional |
| **B. Randomized-arm difference-in-differences (robustness)** | Same ITT, using the change from pre to post by arm | Direct | Same as A; randomization makes parallel trends hold in expectation | Same as A | Less efficient than A when pre and post use are imperfectly correlated | Report alongside A. Large disagreement signals baseline imbalance or a specification problem to investigate, not a reason to choose the more favorable result |
| C. Analyst's single-arm before/after with controls | Change in report-town use over time | **Does not answer it** | Use would have stayed flat without the reports, which the drought order, seasonality and weather contradict | Report-town reads | Confounded by the July 2025 drought order and by time | Not recommended. Its main problem is the confounding by time; its naive SEs also mistake the read count for the number of independent units |
| D. Report towns vs. the 34 non-trial towns | Association | Weak | Non-trial towns comparable to trial towns; they lack smart meters | Billing reads from non-trial towns | Selected, not randomized; different metering | Descriptive only; not needed, because there is a randomized control |

**Primary:** A. **Fallback:** B. **Weakest assumption:** no town-specific
concurrent event by arm. With 12 towns per arm it cannot be diluted, so the
event inventory matters more than any model choice.

**Effect on reading** is not identified (no read data). Treat it as a
future-data option: tracked emails or QR codes in a later rollout.

## 6. Diagnostic, falsification and sensitivity plan

All checks are planned; none has been performed.

| Check | Data | Challenges | Limitation | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomization record audit | Draw record, date, method | Randomization | Cannot detect an undocumented re-draw | If a draw cannot be documented: treat as conditional, disclose, rely on baseline adjustment and placebo checks |
| Baseline comparison by arm (pre-period use, H, L, account counts) | Pre-period reads | Chance imbalance | Balance cannot prove exchangeability; tests on 24 towns have little power | Report it; the primary model adjusts for baseline use; do not re-specify after seeing outcomes |
| Placebo trial date: pretend reports began Mar 2024 (baseline Mar 2023 – Feb 2024, outcome Mar 2024 – Feb 2025) | Pre-period reads | Arm differences in trends before treatment | A null placebo does not prove the absence of a post-period shock | Investigate which towns drive it; report the primary result with this caveat |
| Concurrent-event inventory by town | Rates, campaigns, infrastructure events, drought enforcement | No arm-specific shocks | Missing records ≠ no events | Leave affected town(s) out as sensitivity; if a shock is systematic by arm, the ITT is conditional |
| Leave-one-town-out | Primary data | Undue influence of a single town | Not a test of an assumption | Report the range; flag a fragile conclusion |
| Read missingness, estimated reads, meter swaps and household churn by arm and month | Read-status fields, account history | Outcome observation, cohort selection | Equal rates do not prove ignorable missingness | Bounds or sensitivity analysis on missing reads; analyze the baseline cohort including movers' observed months |
| Spillover inquiry (media coverage, shared institutions) | Communications records | No cross-town interference | Use data cannot detect small spillovers | Interpret the ITT as a lower bound on the no-spillover effect if spillover likely reduced control-town use |
| Month-by-month effect profile, pre- vs. post-drought split | Primary data | Effect dynamics (descriptive) | Drought timing not randomized; multiplicity | Report as secondary and descriptive; no causal claim about drought interaction |
| Scale sensitivity: levels vs. log or percent; household-weighted vs. town-weighted means; prespecified handling of extreme users | Primary data | Specification stability | Agreement does not validate identification | Report all prespecified versions |
| Rebate sign-up ITT (secondary outcome) | Rebate records with dates | n/a (secondary estimand) | Does not decompose the use effect | Report separately; no mediation claim without a separate design |

## 7. Implementation handoff

**Estimand.** Requested and proposed: the ITT of mailing reports.
- Population: households in the 24 trial towns.
- Time zero: March 2025; follow-up: Mar 2025 – Feb 2026.
- Outcome: mean monthly metered use per household (units to confirm).
- Primary scale: absolute difference. Secondary: percent of the control-arm
  mean.
- Weighting: each household weighted equally (the board's "household use").
  Report the town-weighted version as sensitivity.

**Sample.**
- Baseline cohort: accounts or premises active in February 2025 in the
  24 towns. The account-vs-premise choice and the treatment of movers are to be
  confirmed (Q3).
- Keep each household's observed follow-up months; do not drop households for
  being absent in some months without the missingness checks.
- Secondary: all households with any follow-up read.
- Exclude non-residential and master-metered accounts if they cannot be tied to
  one household; record the rule before looking at outcomes.

**Keys and fields.**
- Town ID and household ID; read month aligned to the billing cycle. Define
  "March 2025" exposure relative to the first mailing date (Q7).
- Z_T assignment.
- Baseline covariates: pre-period mean use (Mar 2024 – Feb 2025 and
  Mar 2023 – Feb 2024), plus H and L if measured before March 2025.
- Any randomization strata.

**Design and gates.** Stop and return to this memo if any of these occurs:
- The draw record contradicts "12 of 24 at random".
- Control towns received reports or a similar program.
- An arm-specific concurrent event affects several towns.

**Estimator (primary).**
- One row per household: Y_i = mean monthly use over the follow-up months
  observed for that household.
- Regress Y_i on Z_T and the baseline covariates, with any strata included.
- Treatment-effect estimate: the coefficient on Z_T.
- This collapsing avoids modeling autocorrelation in monthly reads. It is
  equivalent in target to a household-month model with month fixed effects if
  that model is weighted to give each household equal weight.

**Inference.**
- Primary: randomization inference that permutes assignment over the actual
  draw design. Under complete randomization that is C(24,12) = 2,704,156
  assignments, enumerable or sampled.
- Test statistic: the adjusted Z_T coefficient.
- Sharp null: no effect for any household.
- Confidence interval by test inversion under a constant additive effect; this
  is an assumption, so state it.
- Secondary: town-clustered standard errors with a small-sample correction
  (e.g., CR2 with adjusted degrees of freedom, or a wild cluster bootstrap).
- **No** household-level or read-level iid standard errors.
- Treat the primary outcome as one prespecified test; label the month-by-month
  and subgroup results as secondary.
- No small-cluster inference source is in this memo's verified list. Verify the
  chosen package's documentation before implementation.

**Robustness.** Candidate B: the randomized-arm DiD on household-month data,
with household and month fixed effects and town-level inference, plus §6.

**Rebate.** The ITT on sign-up is a secondary outcome. Never use it as a
covariate in the primary analysis.

**Tools.**
- Profiling in Polars, pulling extracts from the warehouse.
- Bayesian execution is `not applicable` as primary; the design-based analysis
  is sufficient. If a hierarchical model is wanted later, use
  `recommend-probabilistic-model`, then `bayesian-workflow` (NumPyro/JAX), and
  pass along this memo. A prior does not change the identification above.

**Outputs.**
- ITT point estimate with randomization-inference p-value and interval, and the
  clustered-SE interval.
- Percent effect.
- Placebo-date result.
- Leave-one-town-out range.
- Missingness and churn tables by arm.
- Rebate ITT.

**Claim limits.** The result is the effect of *mailing* reports in the 24
smart-meter towns, during a drought order. It is not the effect of reading
them, not the effect in the other 34 towns, and not the effect without a
drought.

**Prespecification.** Commit this analysis plan, with outcome definitions, the
cohort, covariates and the primary test, before computing any arm comparison
on the follow-up data.

## 8. Sources

- Hernán, M. A., and J. M. Robins (2020). *Causal Inference: What If*.
  https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook. Used for ITT under randomization,
  exchangeability, consistency, not adjusting for post-treatment mediators, and
  selection.
- Perković, E., J. Textor, M. Kalisch, and M. H. Maathuis (2018). JMLR 18,
  16-319. https://jmlr.org/papers/v18/16-319.html. Used for graphical
  adjustment-set criteria (excluding mediators and colliders).
- Lopez Bernal, J., S. Cummins, and A. Gasparrini (2017). PMC5407170. Used for
  why a single-series before/after comparison is vulnerable to concurrent
  shocks such as the drought order.
- **Source gap:** randomization inference and small-cluster corrections are not
  covered by a verified source here. Add a verified primary or official source
  before citing a specific method in the analysis report.

## 9. Open questions and next action

| # | Question | Who can answer | Effect on recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | How exactly were the 12 towns drawn (simple draw, strata or pairs, seed, date, any re-draw)? | Trial owner | Sets the permutation set and covariates; an undocumented draw makes the design conditional |
| Q2 | Did every scheduled mailing go out? Did control towns get any reports or similar conservation messages? Did report content change (e.g., drought messaging)? | Program and mailing vendor | Consistency and the contrast; contamination biases the ITT toward zero |
| Q3 | Is a household an account or a premise? How are movers, new connections and multi-unit or master-metered buildings handled? | Billing team | Cohort definition and selection checks |
| Q4 | When were household size and lot size recorded or updated? | Billing team | Whether they are baseline covariates or must be dropped |
| Q5 | Was the rebate program available identically in all 24 towns? Did the reports advertise it? Sign-up dates? | Conservation program | Confirms the rebate as a mediator inside the ITT; rules out an arm-specific program |
| Q6 | Were drought rules and enforcement the same in all towns? Any town-specific rate changes, campaigns or infrastructure events Mar 2025 – Feb 2026? | Operations, rates team | Concurrent-event threat; leave-out sensitivity |
| Q7 | Read-cycle dates vs. first mailing date; units; estimated reads; meter replacements | Metering team | Exposure timing for early months; outcome quality |
| Q8 | Has anyone already compared arms on follow-up use? | Analyst | Prespecification credibility; disclose if yes |
| Q9 | What decision is this for (continue, expand to 58 towns), and what effect size matters? | Board | Whether the transport question (alternative (d)) needs its own design |

**Next action:** answer Q1–Q3 from records, commit the §7 plan, then implement
it in a fresh session using this memo as the input.
```

The analyst's instinct to use the pre-period data is right. Put it in the model as a baseline covariate within the between-arm comparison (candidate A), or as the DiD check (candidate B), not as a single-arm before/after. The most useful next step is to answer Q1–Q3 from your records and lock the plan before anyone compares the arms on follow-up use.
